content_html:
An apex legends 240 fps pc build is less about raw power and more about balance: a CPU that can push frame rates past the point most games stop scaling, a GPU that never becomes the bottleneck, and a monitor that can actually display what the system produces. Apex Legends is CPU-hungry at high frame rates because of its netcode, physics and player count, so the parts list below is built around keeping frame times smooth, not just the average FPS number high.

What a 240 FPS Apex Legends Build Actually Needs

Hitting 240 fps in Apex Legends consistently – not just in the menu or an empty lobby – means every component in the chain has to clear 240 frames a second without stalling. That includes the CPU's single-core speed, the GPU's ability to render at your chosen resolution, RAM that feeds data fast enough, and a monitor with a matching refresh rate. Drop any one of these and the other three are wasted money.

Resolution matters here too. At 1080p, the CPU does most of the work and a mid-tier GPU can keep up. At 1440p, the GPU share of the workload grows, so holding 240 fps needs a stronger card. Decide your target resolution before you buy, since it changes which part of the budget should get the bigger share.

The CPU: Why It Matters More Than the GPU for Apex

Apex Legends leans harder on single-core and cache performance than most shooters, which is why current-generation AMD and Intel chips with large cache pools tend to post the highest, most stable frame rates in competitive lobbies. A high core-count chip aimed at rendering or production work is not the priority here – clock speed and cache depth matter more than extra cores sitting idle. Pair the CPU with a capable cooler, since thermal throttling under a 40-plus-degree Bahrain summer is the quiet killer of sustained high frame rates. Browse current options on the CPU category page and match the chip to your target resolution rather than buying the most expensive option by default.

Graphics Card Choice for 240 FPS

Apex Legends is not the most demanding game on a GPU, which means you do not need the top-of-stack card to hit 240 fps at 1080p. At 1440p, though, the GPU becomes the limiting factor more often, and a mid-range card that was comfortable at 1080p can start dropping below 240 in busy fights. Pick a card with enough VRAM headroom for texture streaming and ray-traced effects in other titles you play, since a 240 fps Apex build is rarely the only game on the system. Current cards and their tiers are listed on the graphics card category page, where you can compare what fits a 1080p-240fps build against a 1440p-240fps one.

RAM, Motherboard and the Parts That Don't Get Headlines

Memory speed has a measurable effect on Apex Legends frame rates because the engine is sensitive to memory bandwidth and latency. Running RAM at its rated speed, not the motherboard's conservative default, is one of the cheapest frame rate gains available on a build like this – enabling the memory profile in the BIOS after building usually costs nothing and can be worth several frames per second. 32GB across two sticks is the sensible default for a build that will also run background apps, Discord and a browser while gaming. Full kit options are on the RAM category page. The motherboard itself matters less for FPS directly, but a board with good VRM cooling keeps the CPU running its rated boost clocks longer under sustained load, which does feed back into frame-time consistency.

The Monitor Is Not Optional

None of the above matters without a display that can show 240 frames a second. A 240Hz panel is the minimum here, and the response time matters almost as much as the refresh rate – a slow panel smears motion even at a high refresh rate, undoing the benefit of the frame rate you worked to achieve. 1080p 240Hz panels are the most affordable route to the full frame rate; 1440p 240Hz panels exist and look sharper, but need the stronger GPU tier discussed above to actually fill them. Compare current panels on the monitor category page before finalising the GPU tier, since the two decisions are linked.

Storage, Case Airflow and Keeping It Stable

A fast NVMe drive keeps load times and texture streaming quick, but it has little effect on in-match frame rate – treat it as a quality-of-life upgrade rather than a frame rate one. What does affect sustained frame rates in Bahrain's climate is airflow. A build that throttles after twenty minutes of play because the case runs hot will lose frames exactly when a match gets tense. A case with a clear intake-to-exhaust path, two or three case fans, and a CPU cooler sized for the chip you picked will hold boost clocks far longer than a tight, poorly ventilated case, even with air conditioning running.

Frequently Asked Questions

What CPU do I need for a 240 fps Apex Legends build?

You need a current-generation CPU with strong single-core performance and a large cache, since Apex Legends scales more with per-core speed than core count. Pair it with adequate cooling so it holds its boost clock during long sessions, especially in warmer rooms where thermal throttling can quietly cap your frame rate below the target.

Do I need a 1440p GPU to hit 240 fps in Apex Legends?

Not necessarily. At 1080p, a mid-range GPU can usually sustain 240 fps in Apex Legends because the CPU carries most of the load. At 1440p, the GPU does more work, so you need a stronger card to keep frame rates at 240 during busy fights rather than dropping into the 180-200 range.

Is 32GB of RAM enough for this build?

Yes, 32GB across two sticks is enough for Apex Legends plus background apps like Discord, a browser and voice chat software. Running the RAM at its rated speed via the motherboard's memory profile setting matters more for frame rate than simply having extra capacity beyond 32GB.

What monitor refresh rate should I pair with a 240 fps build?

Match the monitor to the frame rate you are building for: a 240Hz panel is the minimum to see any benefit from the extra frames your PC produces. A slower response time panel can undercut the benefit even at the right refresh rate, so check response time figures, not just the Hz number, before buying.

Will this build overheat in a Bahrain summer?

Any build can throttle in a hot room if the case lacks airflow, regardless of how good the parts are. A case with a clear intake-to-exhaust path, a properly sized cooler for the CPU, and air conditioning in the room will keep a 240 fps build running at its rated clocks through the hottest months.

The Bottom Line

A reliable apex legends 240 fps pc build comes down to four decisions made in the right order: pick the resolution first, choose a CPU with strong single-core and cache performance, size the GPU to that resolution rather than buying the biggest card available, and finish with a 240Hz monitor and a case that keeps everything cool in local conditions. Skip any one of those and the frame rate ceiling drops no matter how much you spent elsewhere. Get the balance right and 240 fps is comfortably within reach even at 1080p on a mid-range budget, with 1440p needing the stronger GPU tier to match.
